fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. Jotham stays out of the temple of the LORD (2 Chronicles 27:2). His father Uzziah, Judah's king before him, did go in, and leprosy broke out on his forehead (2 Chronicles 26:16-21). Jotham did what was right just as Uzziah had, and the text adds that he did not enter.

Close, friend, but Jotham does not go in. The text says he did what was right, just as his father Uzziah had done, and then adds, "In addition, he did not enter the temple of the LORD." (2 Chronicles 27:2). Uzziah, Judah's king before him, went in to burn incense and it did not end well (2 Chronicles 26:16-21). So Jotham stays out.

Towers it is, friend! The text says Jotham builds fortresses and towers out in the forests (2 Chronicles 27:4). He builds cities in the hill country of Judah too. Cities in the hills, fortresses and towers in the forests, and Jotham is building all of it.

Altars are a reasonable guess for a king who does right, but that's not the word. Out in the forests Jotham builds "…fortresses and towers…" (2 Chronicles 27:4). The text doesn't mention any altar-building for him. Towers is the word, friend.

Not this time, friend. The text says Jotham "…waged war against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them…" (2 Chronicles 27:5). That's how the war ends: Jotham defeats them. The Ammonites driving him back isn't what the text says.
That's right, friend. Jotham "…was buried in the City of David." (2 Chronicles 27:9). The text says he rested with his fathers and was buried there. The city carries David's name.

The City of Palms is a real name in the Bible too, friend. It's another name for Jericho (Deuteronomy 34:3), and it's not where Jotham is buried. The text says he "…was buried in the City of David." (2 Chronicles 27:9). That's the city in this verse.

That's right, friend. The last verse says, "And his son Ahaz reigned in his place." (2 Chronicles 27:9). The crown passes from Jotham to his son Ahaz. The story isn't over, and I won't spoil what comes next.
